ladder.name: ConfigHub Plugin
ladder.summary: MIT-licensed hooks, launcher, and starters (wrapping a prebuilt local binary) for Claude Code and Codex. Keeps the request with supported setting edits in ~/.confighub (with first-run 30-day Claude transcript backfill and pattern-based credential redaction), zero background processes, and no account.

ladder.name: ConfigHub local hub
ladder.summary: Free local hub on 127.0.0.1 for base, staging, and live environments, durable previews, linked starters across apps, scoped agent keys, and approved delivery.

ladder.name: Shared ConfigHub
ladder.summary: Move current settings and their reasons to a hub teammates and CI can reach. Earlier revisions and delivery connections stay on the original hub.

verified_prompts.title: Can I change this setting back?
verified_prompts.prompt: I'm thinking of undoing our last settings change. Why did we make it, and where does this app use it? Just show me for now.
verified_prompts.observed_result: Fresh chat recovered the request that enabled CACHE for Friday's sale and pointed to the exact code reading CACHE, even while uncommitted.

verified_prompts.title: Can I see the change before I keep it?
verified_prompts.prompt: Show me my app as it is and a local preview with the heading "Evening collection." Give me both links and keep the preview running for tomorrow.
verified_prompts.observed_result: Both URLs ran side by side; a fresh chat in the same app folder found the same running preview without modifying the app's normal settings.

verified_prompts.title: Fix it once. What happens to my other app?
verified_prompts.prompt: Start a cart app from my shop's setup and give the cart an indigo banner. We now offer support every day. Update the shared hours in staging and show me the hours and banner each app serves.
verified_prompts.observed_result: Both apps picked up daily support hours while the shop stayed coral and the cart stayed indigo; production waited for approval.

verified_prompts.title: On Vercel, try a sale cache without changing the live shop
verified_prompts.prompt: Prices change more often during the sale. Try a 30-second price cache in a Vercel preview. Show me the cache headers from the preview and the live shop. Leave the production change for me to approve.
verified_prompts.observed_result: Vercel preview served Cache-Control: public, max-age=30 while production served max-age=60; ConfigHub refused pending production delivery.

verified_prompts.title: On Daytona, throw away the sandbox and keep the experiment
verified_prompts.prompt: The queue spiked. In a disposable Daytona sandbox, run the same jobs at 120 and 240 per batch. Show me the difference and save the change and its reason for review before you delete the sandbox.
verified_prompts.observed_result: 360 items ran in batches of 120, 120, 120 then 240, 120; after deleting the sandbox, a fresh local hub still held the reason, 240 in staging, and 120 in production.

verified_prompts.title: On Unikraft, rehearse an incident notice on the same image
verified_prompts.prompt: Checkout is delayed. Show me our incident notice on Unikraft staging using the same image as production. Read both notices back to me. I'll decide whether to publish it.
verified_prompts.observed_result: Staging served 'Checkout is delayed. Your cart is saved.' while production served 'Orders ship as usual.' on the exact same image digest; production waited for approval.

verified_prompts.title: Open Friday's production settings as a new preview
verified_prompts.prompt: Open Friday’s production settings as a new preview.
verified_prompts.observed_result: With published mini.29 on an attached local Node app using web and Daytona starter defaults, the historical preview queued its job after three attempts. Production kept delivering on attempt four. Both returning clients found the same running preview without its URL. Two older revision dates were seeded in the disposable hub.

start_after_install.prompt: What does ConfigHub remember about a setting we changed here, and why?
Build a small Node app for my neighborhood market. Give it a heading I can change in .env, run it locally and give me the link.
